milestones.title: Decide and prepare
acceptance_criteria: Storage is behind a port and the migration strategy is decided and written

milestones.title: Postgres implementation
acceptance_criteria: A PostgreSQL implementation passes the same tests and a verified migration tool exists

milestones.title: Cutover
acceptance_criteria: Deployment, backup and rollback support the new store and a rehearsal succeeded on a copy

tasks.title: Write the persistence port and decide the driver and migration strategy
tasks.objective: Specify the repository port, choose the PostgreSQL driver and decide how data and downtime are handled
tasks.estimate_rationale: Architectural decisions with unknown deployment constraints: the EC2 host and database hosting are not visible from this workspace

complexity.justification: Cross-cutting design: synchronous better-sqlite3 calls become asynchronous across repositories and routes

scope.justification: A design record; the code changes are in later tasks

duration.justification: Reading eleven call sites and drafting the record; owner review time is not included

risk.justification: Production data and availability depend on this decision

coupling.justification: Every later task consumes the port and schema decided here

evidence: assumption:a managed PostgreSQL is reachable from the EC2 host
confidence.justification: Hosting for PostgreSQL and the downtime budget are unknown

acceptance_criteria: A decision record names the driver, the port methods and the migration and rollback strategy
Open questions about hosting and downtime are listed for the owner

verification.value: review the decision record with the owner
verification.expected: the owner accepts or amends the record

tasks.title: Move repositories behind the port without changing storage
tasks.objective: Introduce the async port and keep the SQLite implementation passing every existing test
tasks.estimate_rationale: Routes in app.ts call repositories synchronously; making the port async touches routes, services and tests together

complexity.justification: A synchronous to asynchronous change across routes, repositories and services that must keep revision conflict semantics

scope.justification: Four source files and the route layer, extensive but behaviour preserving

duration.justification: Eleven call sites in four files plus fixing awaits in every route; tests are few

risk.justification: Revision conflict and delete cascades are easy to break and only one test covers them

coupling.justification: T3 implements the same port and both edit the repository layer

evidence: assumption:no code outside apps/api calls the repositories
confidence.justification: The code was read, but the test suite is thin and there are no route tests

acceptance_criteria: All routes use the async port
The existing API tests pass unchanged against SQLite
No behaviour change is visible to clients

tasks.title: Implement the PostgreSQL schema and repositories
tasks.objective: Provide a PostgreSQL implementation of the port with schema migration and tests equal to the SQLite ones
tasks.estimate_rationale: New schema, driver, migrations and a test harness that needs a database; JSON validity and ON DELETE CASCADE must be reproduced

complexity.justification: Reproducing SQLite semantics (JSON check, cascade, user_version migrations) in a different engine

scope.justification: A complete second storage implementation with its own tests

duration.justification: New driver, schema and test environment; no precedent in this repository

risk.justification: Data integrity: a schema difference corrupts or loses project data

coupling.justification: Implements the port from T2 and defines the schema that T4 targets

evidence: assumption:a docker postgres is available for tests
confidence.justification: No PostgreSQL exists in this workspace to try against

acceptance_criteria: The PostgreSQL implementation passes the same repository tests as SQLite
data_json validity and cascade deletion are enforced in PostgreSQL

tasks.title: Build the data migration and verification tool
tasks.objective: Copy projects and assets from SQLite to PostgreSQL and verify counts and content hashes
tasks.estimate_rationale: One-shot tool with row counts and sha256 comparison; assets also live on the filesystem

complexity.justification: Streaming copy with verification across two engines and a filesystem tree of assets

scope.justification: A new standalone tool and its report format

duration.justification: backup.ts shows the checksum pattern but the copy and verification logic is new

risk.justification: Operates on production data; an unverified copy loses records

coupling.justification: Targets the schema from T3 and shares only that contract

evidence: assumption:the dataset fits in one transaction batch
confidence.justification: Volume and asset size are unknown

acceptance_criteria: The tool reports equal row counts and content hashes for projects and assets on a copy of production data
The tool is idempotent or refuses to run twice

verification.value: run the tool against a copy of the production backup
verification.expected: counts and hashes match and the report says so

tasks.title: Adapt backup, compose and deployment scripts
tasks.objective: Back up PostgreSQL, provide its service or connection in compose, and keep rollback instructions valid
tasks.estimate_rationale: Four deployment files; hosting choice from T1 decides compose and backup commands

complexity.justification: Deployment, backup and rollback semantics change together and are documented only in PowerShell scripts

scope.justification: Five files across application and operations

duration.justification: Scripts are short but cannot be run locally against the real host

risk.justification: Production deployment and rollback of a database engine

coupling.justification: Uses the PostgreSQL implementation from T3 and the deployment files are shared with release flow

evidence: assumption:the compose file is the only deployment descriptor
confidence.justification: The EC2 host cannot be inspected from here

acceptance_criteria: backup.ts produces a restorable PostgreSQL dump plus assets and checksums
rollback.ps1 states how to restore the previous store

verification.value: run the backup and restore it into an empty database
verification.expected: restored row counts equal the source

tasks.title: Rehearse the migration on a copy and write the cutover runbook
tasks.objective: Run the full migration and rollback on a copy and document the cutover steps with timings
tasks.estimate_rationale: A rehearsal on real data with timing and a written runbook; duration depends on data volume

complexity.justification: Coordinates every earlier task under failure scenarios

scope.justification: A runbook and a rehearsal; no new production code

evidence: assumption:production data is small enough for a same-day rehearsal
duration.justification: Depends on a data volume that is not known yet

risk.justification: Defines the actual production cutover procedure

coupling.justification: Needs the migration tool and the adapted deployment scripts

evidence: assumption:rehearsal runs on EC2 with the same disk
confidence.justification: Durations are unknown until the first rehearsal

acceptance_criteria: The runbook lists every cutover and rollback step with a measured duration from the rehearsal
The rehearsal report shows verified counts and hashes

verification.value: execute the runbook on a copy of production
verification.expected: both complete and the verification report is attached
